mechanism_card.hypothesis: R0's traversal-tail dots (the last 5% of the parent's own FIFO-BFS selection order) still carry unique kernel credit on short late-visited strands, so removing them lowers DTI slightly rather than releasing false-positive mass.
mechanism_card.mechanism: DTI = T / (0.2T + 0.2(S-M) + 0.8|G|). Dropping a dot removes 1 from S (helping the 0.2(S-M) term) but deletes its max-kernel credit wherever it was the best coverer of a truth pixel (hurting T). The parent's recorded recipe ranks its dots by 8-connected FIFO-BFS traversal of the H19-5 support; the dropped tranche is the lowest-priority tail (visit ranks 114510-121128 of 0-121128, n=1,883 of 37,654).
mechanism_card.non_fault_confounder: FIFO-BFS order is a raster convention (seeds at the first raster pixel of each 8-connected support component), not geological confidence: tail dots are the far ends of long lineaments and late chips, where drainage divides and lithologic contacts mimic fault strands. The local report-only PROXYs lean the same sign (catalogue hide-and-recover delta -0.0003; SGMC control delta -0.008), but SGMC-mapped faults are not the new-fault truth and neither PROXY is a score.

mechanism_card.mechanism: Added cells are the next-ranked suppressed H19-5 support cells in the parent's own FIFO-BFS order. Measured: 99.5% of them lie within 2.8 px of an existing R0 dot (median 1.0 px), i.e. exactly the pixels the parent's greedy 2.8 px rule did not keep. Under the metric algebra a dot pays only if its marginal kernel credit exceeds ~0.2*DTI (about 0.056 at 0.28; lower for line-like truth). Redundant neighbours add S but little T and M.
mechanism_card.non_fault_confounder: Dense multiscale ridge corridors (drainage divides, lithologic contacts, foliation lineaments) populate H19-5's suppressed cells. The opposite confounder: real fault zones are damage-zone wide and can carry several parallel strands inside the 300 m kernel, so genuinely useful adds look redundant and new-fault truth can sit within 300 m of known traces (organizer forum, 2026-10-22).
